servcat

servcat provides an R interface to ServCat, the authoritative repository for U.S. Fish and Wildlife Service (FWS) data and reference information.

Use this package to search ServCat, retrieve reference metadata, inspect related units and subject categories, access saved collections, and download files associated with ServCat references.

Installation

You can install the development version of servcat from GitHub with:

# install.packages("pak")
pak::pak("USFWS/servcat")

Then load the package:

library(servcat)

Usage

Search for references by their ID

ServCat references have unique reference IDs. If you already know the reference ID, you can retrieve the reference record directly.

ref <- get_reference(140411)

ref

This is useful when you want to inspect metadata for a known ServCat item, such as title, abstract, publication date, authors, associated files, or related organizational information.

Run an advanced search

Use advanced_search() to search ServCat with one or more search criteria. Search criteria are sent in the body of a POST request, while paging options control how many records are returned.

results <- advanced_search(
  criteria = list(
    quickSearch = "Kodiak goats"
  ),
  page = 1,
  page_size = 25
)

results

You can combine multiple criteria in the request body:

results <- advanced_search(
  criteria = list(
    quickSearch = "wetlands",
    title = "inventory",
    subjectCategories = c("Habitat", "Wetlands")
  ),
  page = 1,
  page_size = 50
)

The exact fields available for advanced search depend on the ServCat API. Common criteria may include text search terms, title keywords, author names, subject categories, reference types, organizations, dates, and geographic filters.

Return composite advanced search results

Some ServCat endpoints return additional composite detail for each reference. Use composite search when you need richer results than the standard advanced search response.

composite_results <- advanced_search(
  criteria = list(
    quickSearch = "Kodiak, goats"
  ),
  page = 1,
  page_size = 25,
  composite = TRUE
)

composite_results

Composite results may include additional nested information about the reference, such as related files, organizations, people, subjects, or other associated metadata.

Retrieve references from a saved collection

ServCat saved collections group related references. Use get_collection_references() with a saved collection ID to retrieve the references in that collection.

collection_refs <- get_collection_references(1397)

collection_refs

This is useful when working with curated groups of references, such as project collections, regional datasets, or topic-based ServCat collections.

Download files from a reference

Many ServCat references include one or more associated files. Use download_reference_files() to download files attached to a reference.

download_reference_files(
  reference_id = 140411,
  path = "data-raw/servcat-files"
)

You can also use this function in a loop or with lapply()/purrr::map() to download files from multiple references.

reference_ids <- c(140411, 140412, 140413)

lapply(
  reference_ids,
  download_reference_files,
  path = "data-raw/servcat-files"
)

Get units associated with a reference

ServCat references can be associated with one or more FWS units. Use get_reference_units() to retrieve those units.

units <- get_reference_units(140411)

units

Get geographic bounding boxes

Use get_reference_bounding_boxes() to retrieve geographic bounding box coordinates associated with a reference.

bbox <- get_reference_bounding_boxes(140411)

bbox

Bounding boxes can help identify the geographic extent of a reference and may be useful for mapping or spatial filtering workflows.

Get subject categories

Use get_reference_subjects() to retrieve the subject categories associated with a ServCat reference.

subjects <- get_reference_subjects(140411)

subjects

Subject categories can help classify references by topic and support more targeted searches.

Get reference types

Use get_reference_types() to retrieve the list of ServCat reference types.

reference_types <- get_reference_types()

reference_types

Reference types can be useful when building advanced searches or filtering results to particular kinds of records.

Example workflow

A typical workflow might look like this:

library(servcat)

# Search ServCat
results <- advanced_search(
  criteria = list(
    quickSearch = "Kodiak goats"
  ),
  page = 1,
  page_size = 10,
  composite = TRUE
)

# Inspect one reference ID from the results
ref <- get_reference(140411)

# Retrieve related metadata
units <- get_reference_units(140411)
subjects <- get_reference_subjects(140411)
bbox <- get_reference_bounding_boxes(140411)

# Download associated files
download_reference_files(
  reference_id = 140411,
  path = "data-raw/servcat-files"
)

Notes

servcat wraps the ServCat REST API and returns R objects suitable for downstream analysis, reporting, and data management workflows.

Because ServCat records can vary in structure, some returned fields may be missing, empty, or nested depending on the reference, endpoint, and search type used.

Getting help

Contact a project maintainer for help with this repository.

If you have general questions on creating repositories in the USFWS DGEC, reach out to a USFWS DGEC owner.

Contribute

Contact the project maintainer for information about contributing to this repository.

Submit a GitHub Issue to report a bug or request a feature or enhancement.

When reporting an issue, please include:

  • A brief description of the problem.
  • A minimal reproducible example, if possible.
  • The function you were using.
  • The ServCat reference ID, collection ID, or search criteria involved.
  • Your R version and servcat package version.
